newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All newspapers
LEGAL NET TIGHTENS AROUND FORMER PM RAO

A special court indicted former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a vote-buying case, dealing another legal setback to the embattled politician who quit in disgrace last year as Congress party leader. The judge ruled that there was sufficient evidence to try Rao for criminal conspiracy and abetment to bribery, the counsel for the former prime minister said.
The Economic Times
APEX BANK DISCLOSURE TO OUTWIT ERRANT PLAYERS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is considering adopting a disclosure policy under which it will make public the list of institutions against whom action has been taken. A decision in this regard is being deliberated within the RBI at the highest level. Once implemented, the errant players' run-ins with the RBI would no longer be a secret between them and the central bank.
HFC CAN CLASSIFY NPAS FOR THREE QUARTERS

The National Housing Bank relaxed classification norms for non performing assets of housing finance companies (HFCs) from two quarters to three quarters. It also allowed HFCs a zero percent risk weightage on housing and project loans guaranteed by either the state or central governments for determining capital adequacy. The moves will help weaker HFCs tide over difficult times, sources said. However, Housing Development Finance Corporation will not be affected by the changes as it had already announced results based on old provisioning norms.
SAMSUNG REAFFIRMS COMMITMENT TO INDIA

Samsung Electronic Company is going ahead with its plans to set up a wholly-owned holding company in India. The holding company, originally scheduled to have been set up by the end of 1996, would be the conduit for channelling investments for its new projects in India. Samsung, awaiting clearance from the government, has made an investment proposal of $630 million until the end of 1998. Samsung has a presence in the white goods segment with a 51:49 joint venture. It also has a presence in the telecom systems market through a joint venture with Larsen & Toubro.
Financial Express
PRIME MINISTER TO SIGN OIL PRICE HIKE NOTE THIS WEEK

Prime Minister I.K. Gujral, who also holds the petroleum portfolio, is expected to approve a draft cabinet note on oil price hike by the end of the week. A cabinet note, attempting a roughly 15 percent increase in the price of petroleum products, is being drafted to enable the government to announce a hike by the end of the month. The proposal, which greatly modified the Petroleum Ministry's first plan of a 30 percent hike, is already in circulation.
COMPANIES CAN TAP PUBLIC FUNDS FOR BUYBACK

The companies will be allowed to tap the public for funds to buy back their shares from the market, according to the working draft of the Companies Bill. The earlier draft restricted the resource mobilisation for such buybacks from either the share premium account or free reserves. The draft, however, did not elaborate on the instruments that could be used to mop up public money for buyback.
PROFIT MAKING GOVERNMENT UNITS GET MORE TEETH

The government enhanced the powers of profit-making public enterprises to incur capital expenditure without its prior approval. The Board of Enterprises could sanction expenditure up to one billion rupees without prior approval provided the undertaking had shown profits in each of the preceding three accounting years and had a positive net worth.
SLOWDOWN IN SCOOTER SEGMENT DENTS BAJAJ NET

Bajaj Auto's profit after tax (PAT) for 1996/97 (April-March) was around three percent more than the previous year's figure of 4.18 billion rupees. Company sources admitted it was in the range of 4.25 billion rupees to 4.3 billion rupees. The PAT fell short of analysts' expectations who had estimated it to be 4.6 billion rupees on the assumption that sales of two and three-wheelers would be 1.46 million units. However, Bajaj Auto sold 1.43 million vehicles, with sales in the second half of 1996/97 not as buoyant as in the first.
Business Standard
VOLVO PROJECT MAY BE EXEMPTED FROM EXPORT OBLIGATION

The Directorate-General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) is willing to consider a request by Swedish automobiles major Volvo to exempt the company from export obligations in exchange for permission to import equipment. Volvo has been asked to submit a proposal for relaxation of the extent of indigenisation and export obligations imposed on the company under the memorandum of understanding (MoU) it will have to sign with the government. The DGFT was willing to consider an exemption since Volvo was seeking an MoU for the high-powered transport sector rather than the luxury car sector.
10 BLN RUPEE COMMERCIAL PAPERS SLATED TO HIT MARKET

Commercial paper worth 10 billion rupees was slated to hit the market in the next few months with interest rates dropping and subscribers willing to pick up the instrument without a stand by facility. On April 15, 1996, the total outstanding commercial papers stood at 7.05 billion rupees. These three month papers carried interest rates in the band of 11.3 percent and 12.5 percent. Currently the interest rates on these 90-day papers are in the 10.5 percent to 12 percent range depending on the profile of the company.
SIX POINT PLAN TO REFORM SUBSIDY REGIME

The government suggested a six-point strategy for reforming the subsidies regime, which stood at 1,373.38 billion rupees, or 14.4 percent of gross domestic product in 1994/95 (April-March). The state government's share amounted to 940 billion rupees. According to the white paper prepared by the Finance Ministry, subsidies on merit goods like education and roads and bridges accounted for less than a third of the states' subsidy bill. The paper suggested increasing user charges on non-merit goods like power, transport, irrigation, agriculture and higher education to enable the nation halve the current subsidy rate of over 90 percent.
NEW AIR INDIA, INDIAN AIRLINES PACT TO PAVE WAY FOR MERGER

The Civil Aviation Ministry unveiled a comprehensive guideline for code sharing between Indian Airlines and Air-India which was expected to pave the way for the merger of the two airlines. A coordination committee was assigned to monitor the implementation of the guideline. Once the norms were implemented, both the airlines would merely be a step away from merger. However, the implementation could be delayed with the airlines differing on the terms of the draft guideline circulated earlier.
